assumptions: One task, two writers and tenants, versions 1..6, clock 0..4, three history elements and two import fingerprints.
CAS retries, expiry and deletion, owner filtering and pre-serving idempotent import are modeled.

Arbitrary unconditional replacement, the Redis backend and semantic task status transitions are excluded. Ten real SQLite-backed workerd checks cover selected receipt and content-preservation scenarios, not general trace equivalence.
A foreign read is rejected before the owned import phase closes, matching the Durable Object transaction.

History is set-valued in this model. Real implementation checks assert ordered complete content and duplicate retention. Multi-task import conflict atomicity is checked by workerd outside the one-task model.
bounds.progress: The storage projection permits stuttering and repeated failures and makes no progress claim.
terminalCancellation: One authorized organization and task, two admitted cancel requests and at most one completion publication of a working record. A version conflict re-reads, and the terminal check prevents another mutation. The successful cancellation reply represents the acknowledged stored version.

Completion carries symbolic complete history and one artifact. Real Hono/Workerd checks hold an actual SQLite read receipt across completion or another cancellation. They check exact terminal output and successful/refused conditional writes with a local authenticated principal.

One optional completion can race the observed working task. Arbitrary later message/send replacements, independent raw history or artifact appends, expiration, deletion and recreation during a semantic cancel, lost write acknowledgements, the legacy skill lifecycle and Redis lock expiry are outside this projection. The storage projection separately checks bounded TTL and import behavior.

assumptions: No fairness. At most one completion publication is enabled while the task is working. Independent appends, expiry and later unconditional replacements are outside this projection.

Weak fairness of read and conditional write replies for both admitted cancels. Reads and writes respond; a version conflict is possible once and causes a fresh read. Uncertain effects and storage outages are outside this progress claim.
No fairness. A ready read or write can remain pending.
